children: U.S. stocks moved higher Thursday as investors assessed economic data and Treasury yields eased following the Federal Reserve's first interest-rate increase in more than three years.

The Nasdaq Composite climbed about 1.5%, while the S&P 500 gained roughly 1.3% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added about 0.8%. The advance followed a weaker session on Wednesday after policymakers lifted the federal funds rate by 25 basis points and indicated additional tightening could remain possible.

Fresh economic reports painted a mixed picture. Weekly jobless claims declined, suggesting labor-market conditions remained relatively firm. At the same time, housing starts and building permits fell, pointing to continued pressure in the housing sector amid elevated borrowing costs.

Bond markets also stabilized. The two-year Treasury yield slipped to around 4.72%, while the benchmark 10-year yield eased to near 5%, retreating from recent highs. Lower yields appeared to support appetite for technology and growth shares during the session.
Markets continue to weigh the impact of tighter monetary policy against signs that economic activity remains resilient.

title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq Jump After Fed Delivers First Rate Hike in Years
